collection.label: Herodotus on the kings of Egypt
collection.critical_edition: Greek of A. D. Godley's Loeb edition (1920), via Perseus
collection.search_terms: herodotus histories book 2 egypt kings min menes sesostris proteus helen rhampsinitus cheops chephren mycerinus pyramids sethos 341 generations 11340 years sun rose west
collection.description: Herodotus' account of the kings of Egypt from Min to Sethos, as the priests of Memphis told it, and their chronology of 341 generations and 11,340 years, on the pages of the oldest manuscript of the Histories (Florence, Laur. Plut. 70.3, 10th c.).

texts.title: Herodotus, Histories 2.99-101: Min, Nitocris and the 330 kings
texts.source: Florence, Laur. Plut. 70.3 (10th c.) via BML Teca Digitale + Greek of Godley's Loeb (Perseus) + English of A. D. Godley (1920, Wikisource, checked against the printing)
texts.description: Herodotus begins the Egyptian priests' history of their kings: Min, the first king, who dammed the Nile and founded Memphis; the 330 kings after him read out from a papyrus roll, among them the queen Nitocris; and Moeris, who built the lake.

texts.title: Herodotus, Histories 2.102-110: Sesostris, the conqueror king
texts.source: Florence, Laur. Plut. 70.3 (10th c.) via BML Teca Digitale + Greek of Godley's Loeb (Perseus) + English of A. D. Godley (1920, Wikisource, checked against the printing)
texts.description: The campaigns of Sesostris by sea and land through Asia and into Europe, the pillars he set up, the Colchians as Egyptian settlers, the plot of his brother at Daphnae, the canals dug by his captives, and his statues at the temple of Hephaestus.

texts.title: Herodotus, Histories 2.111: Pheros, the blind king
texts.source: Florence, Laur. Plut. 70.3 (10th c.) via BML Teca Digitale + Greek of Godley's Loeb (Perseus) + English of A. D. Godley (1920, Wikisource, checked against the printing)
texts.description: Pheros, son of Sesostris, who threw a spear into the flooding Nile, was struck blind for ten years, and recovered his sight as the oracle of Buto foretold.

texts.title: Herodotus, Histories 2.112-120: Proteus, and Helen in Egypt
texts.source: Florence, Laur. Plut. 70.3 (10th c.) via BML Teca Digitale + Greek of Godley's Loeb (Perseus) + English of A. D. Godley (1920, Wikisource, checked against the printing)
texts.description: The priests' account of Proteus of Memphis, who detained Helen and the stolen treasure when Paris was driven to Egypt, of Menelaus' visit, and Herodotus' argument that Homer knew this version and that Helen was never at Troy.

texts.title: Herodotus, Histories 2.121-123: Rhampsinitus, the treasure-thief, and the descent to the underworld
texts.source: Florence, Laur. Plut. 70.3 (10th c.) via BML Teca Digitale + Greek of Godley's Loeb (Perseus) + English of A. D. Godley (1920, Wikisource, checked against the printing)
texts.description: Rhampsinitus and the tale of the builder's sons who robbed his treasury, his journey alive to the underworld where he played dice with Demeter, and the Egyptian teaching on the immortality and migration of the soul.

texts.title: Herodotus, Histories 2.124-128: Cheops and Chephren, the builders of the pyramids
texts.source: Florence, Laur. Plut. 70.3 (10th c.) via BML Teca Digitale + Greek of Godley's Loeb (Perseus) + English of A. D. Godley (1920, Wikisource, checked against the printing)
texts.description: Cheops, who closed the temples and set all Egyptians to building the Great Pyramid, its construction by stages and its cost in radishes, onions and garlic, and his brother Chephren's pyramid; 106 years of oppression.

texts.title: Herodotus, Histories 2.129-135: Mycerinus, the oracle of six years, and Rhodopis
texts.source: Florence, Laur. Plut. 70.3 (10th c.) via BML Teca Digitale + Greek of Godley's Loeb (Perseus) + English of A. D. Godley (1920, Wikisource, checked against the printing)
texts.description: Mycerinus, who reopened the temples and judged justly, his daughter buried in a golden cow at Sais, the oracle that gave him six more years, his pyramid, and the story of the courtesan Rhodopis.

texts.title: Herodotus, Histories 2.136: Asychis and the brick pyramid
texts.source: Florence, Laur. Plut. 70.3 (10th c.) via BML Teca Digitale + Greek of Godley's Loeb (Perseus) + English of A. D. Godley (1920, Wikisource, checked against the printing)
texts.description: Asychis, who built the eastern gateway of the temple of Hephaestus, made a law of loans on the security of a father's mummy, and built a pyramid of brick.

texts.title: Herodotus, Histories 2.137-140: Anysis the blind and Sabacos the Ethiopian
texts.source: Florence, Laur. Plut. 70.3 (10th c.) via BML Teca Digitale + Greek of Godley's Loeb (Perseus) + English of A. D. Godley (1920, Wikisource, checked against the printing)
texts.description: The blind king Anysis, the fifty-year rule of the Ethiopian Sabacos who raised the cities on mounds, his dream and withdrawal, and Anysis' return from the marshes.

texts.title: Herodotus, Histories 2.141: Sethos and the army of Sennacherib
texts.source: Florence, Laur. Plut. 70.3 (10th c.) via BML Teca Digitale + Greek of Godley's Loeb (Perseus) + English of A. D. Godley (1920, Wikisource, checked against the printing)
texts.description: Sethos, priest of Hephaestus, whose army of shopkeepers and craftsmen faced Sennacherib at Pelusium, where mice gnawed the enemy's quivers, bowstrings and shield-straps in the night.

texts.title: Herodotus, Histories 2.142-146: The priests' chronology: 341 generations and 11,340 years
texts.source: Florence, Laur. Plut. 70.3 (10th c.) via BML Teca Digitale + Greek of Godley's Loeb (Perseus) + English of A. D. Godley (1920, Wikisource, checked against the printing)
texts.description: The priests' reckoning from the first king to Sethos: 341 generations of kings and high priests, 11,340 years without a god in human form, in which the sun four times rose out of its usual place; the 345 wooden statues shown to Hecataeus at Thebes; and the ages of Heracles, Dionysus and Pan.
